cues.en: Hello, and welcome to BSD TV. This is a recording of the talk Scott Long gave at the twenty fourteen NYC BSD Con entitled serving one third of the Internet via free BSD.
cues.zh: 大家好，欢迎收看 BSD TV。这是 Scott Long 在 2014 年纽约 BSD 大会上所作演讲的录像，演讲题目是《通过 FreeBSD 为三分之一的互联网提供服务》。

cues.en: In this talk, Scott covers the impressive infrastructure the five person team has built over at Netflix
cues.zh: 在演讲中，Scott 介绍了 Netflix 五人团队搭建的强大基础设施，

cues.en: and how they are giving back to the community. With their robust system, the team over at Netflix has been able to throw enough total processing power and traffic at the systems in a single weekend to generate errors that would take months to show up in other production environments.
cues.zh: 以及他们如何回馈社区。凭借稳健的系统，Netflix 团队能在一个周末内向系统施加足够大的总处理能力和流量，触发一些在其他生产环境中可能要几个月才会出现的错误。

cues.en: We are certainly glad to have such a powerhouse in our corner.
cues.zh: 有你们这样的强援支持，我们真的很高兴。

cues.en: I hope you enjoy it. There's a lot of new faces here that I haven't seen before. I've I've been to a bunch of conferences recently,
cues.zh: 希望你们喜欢。这里有很多我之前没见过的新面孔。我最近参加了一堆会议，

cues.en: George said there's gonna be a lot of new people here, so I figured I'd talk about myself just very briefly.
cues.zh: George说会有很多新人来，所以我想简单介绍一下自己。

cues.en: I've been with Netflix for about a year and a half now. Before that, I was with I was with Yahoo on their kernel team. As you know, until
cues.zh: 我在Netflix待了大约一年半了。在那之前，我在Yahoo的内核团队。如你所知，直到

cues.en: fairly recently, Yahoo was pretty much powered by by FreeBSD.
cues.zh: 不久前，Yahoo基本上还是靠FreeBSD支撑的。

cues.en: I've done a lot of work with storage companies, with SAS, SATA, old SCSI, ATA, that kind of stuff. I've also worked a little bit with networking and security.
cues.zh: 我和很多存储公司合作过，接触过 SAS、SATA、老式 SCSI、ATA 之类的技术。我也做过一些网络和安全方面的工作。

cues.en: And all told, I've been using FreeBSD
cues.zh: 总的来说，我用 FreeBSD 已经

cues.en: for
cues.zh: 有

cues.en: twenty one years, even before it was called FreeBSD back in three zero six BSD days,
cues.zh: 二十一年了，早在它还叫三零六 BSD 的时候，也就是

cues.en: I've been a FreeBSD committer since 2000. I was the release engineer from 2002 to 2006,
cues.zh: 从 2000 年起，我就是 FreeBSD 提交者。2002 年到 2006 年，我担任发行工程师，

cues.en: back during the
cues.zh: 那时正值

cues.en: FreeBSD five, FreeBSD six days of kinda digging ourselves out of that hole and and getting three sixty on the right track.
cues.zh: FreeBSD 5 和 FreeBSD 6 的时期，我们正努力从那个困境中走出来，让三六零回到正轨。

cues.en: And also,
cues.zh: 还有，

cues.en: my degree is actually in aviation science. I was actually a commercial pilot for a little while, so that's
cues.zh: 我的学位其实是航空科学。我 actually 当过一段时间的商业飞行员，所以那是我

cues.en: what I do for fun.
cues.zh: 消遣的方式。

cues.en: Anyway, so I wanna talk about Netflix streaming.
cues.zh: 总之，我想谈谈 Netflix 流媒体。

cues.en: Not terribly technical,
cues.zh: 不太偏技术，

cues.en: wanted to focus more on the big picture of what we do at Netflix and how we use FreeBSD and how it's been successful for us.
cues.zh: 更想聚焦于我们在 Netflix 做事情的大局，以及我们如何使用 FreeBSD，还有它如何为我们带来成功。

cues.en: As you may or may not know or seen previous presentations, we are responsible for about a third of the Internet's traffic here in North America
cues.zh: 你们可能知道也可能不知道，或者看过之前的演讲，我们在北美占了大约三分之一的互联网流量

cues.en: and that is almost all on FreeBSD right now. So
cues.zh: 而现在这几乎全部跑在 FreeBSD 上。所以

cues.en: thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: So there's three big pieces to Netflix streaming. What I mean by streaming is traditionally Netflix was was singing out DVDs by mail. We had this great infrastructure for getting you DVDs quickly and
cues.zh: Netflix 的流媒体业务主要由三大部分组成。过去，Netflix 通过邮寄 DVD 来提供服务。我们搭建了一套很棒的基础设施，能快速把 DVD 寄给你，

cues.en: offering suggestions on what you might like and building this big pipeline so that you could watch movies very efficiently
cues.zh: 向你推荐可能喜欢的内容，并打造了一条完整的流程，让你能高效地看电影，

cues.en: and not have to go to Blockbuster and deal with late fees and all that kind of stuff.
cues.zh: 不用跑去百视达，也不用担心逾期费之类的麻烦。

cues.en: But we started to shift towards streaming a few years ago realizing that
cues.zh: 但几年前，我们开始转向流媒体，意识到

cues.en: the Internet was the future, obviously.
cues.zh: 互联网显然就是未来。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: we learned some of our
cues.zh: 我们从做 DVD 中学到了

cues.en: infrastructure from doing the DVD, a lot of our data science, lot of our website building authentication, all that kind of stuff, Kind of reuse that for the streaming
cues.zh: 一些基础设施经验，很多数据科学、很多网站构建的认证，诸如此类的东西，都复用到流媒体上

cues.en: and added things to it like we do encoding and
cues.zh: 并在此基础上增加了一些功能，比如我们做编码，

cues.en: take the movies from the studios, re encode it, we have to encrypt it, that kind of stuff and doing command and control.
cues.zh: 从制片厂拿到电影，重新编码，还得加密，诸如此类，以及做命令与控制。

cues.en: The second big part is obviously the clients, what you run on your computer or your Roku or whatever.
cues.zh: 第二大部分显然是客户端，也就是你在电脑、Roku 之类的设备上运行的东西。

cues.en: A lot people ask me where is the Linux client, where is the previous D client?
cues.zh: 很多人问我，Linux 客户端在哪里？之前的 D 客户端呢？

cues.en: And best I can say is that HTML5
cues.zh: 我能说的就是，HTML5

cues.en: is something that we've been talking about. It's definitely on our road map. So hopefully,
cues.zh: 一直在我们的讨论范围内，肯定也在我们的路线图上。所以希望，

cues.en: as time goes on, we'll start ditching a lot these custom clients and go towards sandwich based streaming and that kind of stuff.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，我们能逐步淘汰很多定制客户端，转向基于 Sandwich 的流媒体方案之类的东西。

cues.en: But the interesting part for me and my job is the content streaming, actually getting the bits out to your computer.
cues.zh: 但对我来说，工作中真正有趣的部分是内容流式传输，也就是把数据真正传到你的电脑上。

cues.en: Traditionally,
cues.zh: 传统上，

cues.en: we were using the the big three content delivery networks, the Akamai, the LimeWise level threes. And if you're not familiar with how the Internet works,
cues.zh: 我们用的是三大内容分发网络：Akamai、Limelight、Level 3。如果你不熟悉互联网的运作方式，

cues.en: these are the companies that
cues.zh: 这些公司

cues.en: basically cache all the all the all the images and and big objects and small objects, all all the stuff that you you see on your web page, lot of that comes from these companies that they cache these objects out in ISPs and and at network interchange points across the country and across the world. When you connect to a website, when you go to google.com,
cues.zh: 基本上会缓存所有的图片、大大小小的对象，你在网页上看到的大量内容都来自这些公司——它们把这些对象缓存到各地的ISP和全国乃至全世界的网络交换点上。当你连接一个网站、访问google.com时，

cues.en: you may not be reaching a server in California, you might be reaching a server that's here in New York City or up in Boston or Chicago or something like that and
cues.zh: 你可能连到的并不是加州的服务器，而可能是纽约市、波士顿或芝加哥等地的服务器，

cues.en: getting cached content. That content usually comes from these big CDNs.
cues.zh: 获取缓存内容。这些内容通常来自大型 CDN。

cues.en: We were using those CDNs at Netflix to
cues.zh: 我们以前在 Netflix 用这些 CDN

cues.en: cash and deliver all of our movies for a long time but we basically outgrew them. When you're dealing with a third of the Internet and hopefully beyond,
cues.zh: 来缓存和传送所有影片，持续了很长一段时间，但后来我们的规模超出了它们的承载能力。我们处理的流量占整个互联网的三分之一，而且还希望继续扩大，

cues.en: they couldn't keep up with us. So we decided that we were gonna make our own content delivery network and we called it Open Connect.
cues.zh: 它们已经跟不上我们了。所以我们决定自建内容分发网络，并将它命名为 Open Connect。

cues.en: So, what is Open Connect? It's basically
cues.zh: 那么，Open Connect 是什么？它基本上就是

cues.en: a web server.
cues.zh: 一台 Web 服务器。

cues.en: In the most basic sense, we have a box that's web server.
cues.zh: 最基本来说，我们有一个盒子，那就是Web服务器。

cues.en: Each web URL is a movie or it's a video stream and audio stream.
cues.zh: 每个网页URL就是一部电影，或者是一个视频流和音频流。

cues.en: And our job is to make that
cues.zh: 我们的工作就是把它做成

cues.en: a very reliable,
cues.zh: 一个非常可靠、

cues.en: very fast,
cues.zh: 非常快、

cues.en: very scalable system.
cues.zh: 非常有扩展性的系统。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: we do it basically taking off the shelf components.
cues.zh: 我们基本上是采用现成的组件来做。

cues.en: We're not building super duper special
cues.zh: 我们不是在造超级特别的

cues.en: high performance machines.
cues.zh: 高性能机器。

cues.en: You know, we're not building massive terabit memory systems and and and all that kind of stuff. We're using basically off the shelf components,
cues.zh: 你知道，我们不是在造大规模的太比特内存系统之类的东西。我们基本上用的是现成组件，

cues.en: off the shelf software.
cues.zh: 现成的软件。

cues.en: We're
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: packaging it into machines that are friendly to put into ISPs because we really want ISPs to take our machines and I'll talk about that in a second.
cues.zh: 把它打包成对ISP友好的机器，因为我们真的很希望ISP能采用我们的机器，我稍后会讲到这一点。

cues.en: And where we can't put into ISPs, we're putting it into interchanges, into places like,
cues.zh: 在无法进入ISP的地方，我们就把它部署到交换中心，部署到像

cues.en: I can't remember the interchange here in New York, but
cues.zh: 我记不清纽约这里的交换中心了，但是

cues.en: the big peering points around the country so that we are close to the customers and close to big ISPs.
cues.zh: 全国各大对等互联点，这样我们就能靠近客户，靠近大型ISP。

cues.en: And I'm gonna talk quite a bit about this but if you wanna
cues.zh: 我会详细讲这一点，但如果你想

cues.en: look up more online, we have a website, openconnect.netflix.com.
cues.zh: 在网上了解更多，我们有一个网站，openconnect.netflix.com。

cues.en: I'll warn you, it's a little bit out of date, I'm behind on updating it but it does give you some background into specifics of our vendors and our architecture and that kind of stuff. So you're welcome to go read that in parallel here if you want.
cues.zh: 我得提醒一下，这份材料有点过时了，我还没来得及更新，但它确实能让你了解我们供应商的具体情况和架构之类的东西。所以你如果有兴趣，可以一边听一边去看看。

cues.en: So like I said,
cues.zh: 就像我说的，

cues.en: the way the Internet works these days is that you're no longer getting all your content from that endpoint website that you thought you went to, you're gaining it from caches along the way.
cues.zh: 如今互联网的运作方式是，你不再是从你以为访问的那个终点网站获取所有内容，而是从沿途的缓存中获取。

cues.en: And this diagram kind of lays out what our network looks like.
cues.zh: 这张图大致展示了我们的网络架构。

cues.en: Amazon is our source of truth where all the data comes from originally. That's where we do all of our encoding and
cues.zh: Amazon 是我们的数据源头，所有数据最初都来自这里。我们在这里完成所有编码工作，还有

cues.en: like
cues.zh: 类似

cues.en: that kind of stuff.
cues.zh: 这类事情。

cues.en: But then we push it out to this here architecture
cues.zh: 然后我们把数据推送到这个架构中

cues.en: of origin servers, interchange servers,
cues.zh: 包括源站服务器、互联服务器，

cues.en: embedded servers that
cues.zh: 以及嵌入式服务器，它们

cues.en: are at the network interchange points that are inside the ISPs.
cues.zh: 位于 ISP 内部的网络互联节点。

cues.en: And the idea is that the client can connect to any one of these points
cues.zh: 我们的想法是，客户端可以连接到其中任意一个节点

cues.en: to get the movie and
cues.zh: 来获取影片，而且

cues.en: there's a lot of logic that's put into what we call our control backplane to help clients choose the best server for them to go to,
cues.zh: 我们在称为控制平面的系统中加入了很多逻辑，帮助客户端选择最适合连接的服务器，

cues.en: whether it's a cache inside the ISP that has their movie
cues.zh: 可能是 ISP 内部缓存着这部影片的服务器，

cues.en: or maybe all the local caches are busy and they need to leave the local caches and go up a higher tier.
cues.zh: 也可能本地缓存都很忙，客户端需要离开本地缓存，转到更高一层。

cues.en: All that kind of steering is done
cues.zh: 这些调度都在

cues.en: in the background
cues.zh: 后台完成，

cues.en: but all using the same machines.
cues.zh: 但用的都是同样的机器。

cues.en: And like I said, one
cues.zh: 就像我说的，

cues.en: of the big reasons we're doing this is because we outgrew the big three CDNs.
cues.zh: 我们这么做的一大原因，是三大 CDN 已经不够我们用了。

cues.en: They just had
cues.zh: 他们对我们

cues.en: no more capacity for us.
cues.zh: 已经没有更多容量了。

cues.en: But also we're trying to do this to save money for ourselves and for our customers and for the ISPs because
cues.zh: 但我们这么做也是想为自己、为我们的客户和 ISP 省钱，因为

cues.en: it's been a big complaint that since we are such a large portion of the Internet that video streaming
cues.zh: 一直有很大的抱怨：我们在互联网中占比这么大，视频流媒体

cues.en: has become such a big thing in the Internet just in the past five years
cues.zh: 在过去五年里成了互联网中的重头戏，

cues.en: that we're breaking a lot of ISPs cost models that
cues.zh: 我们打破了很多 ISP 的成本模型，

cues.en: were causing their customers to pull in a lot more bits than they traditionally were budgeted for.
cues.zh: 导致他们的客户拉取的比特量远超传统预算。

cues.en: So we really want to get
cues.zh: 我们确实希望把

cues.en: caches into
cues.zh: 缓存放进

cues.en: these ISPs so that the customer doesn't have to weave their boundary and go up to transit in order to get the bits. The customer can stay entirely within the ISP and basically operate for free.
cues.zh: 这些 ISP 里，这样客户就不必绕出网络边界、连接到上游转接网络来获取数据。客户可以完全留在 ISP 内，基本上免费使用。

cues.en: And the caches that we produce, we
cues.zh: 我们提供的缓存设备，

cues.en: give to ISPs for free. There are some requirements in terms of expected bandwidth, expected usage.
cues.zh: 会免费交给 ISP 使用，但对带宽和预期使用量有一些要求。

cues.en: These machines aren't free for us both in terms of upfront cost and in terms of administration, so we have to be a little bit selective about ISPs but at the same time, we still are working very hard to get our caches out to as many ISPs as possible,
cues.zh: 这些设备对我们来说并非没有成本，包括前期费用和管理成本，所以我们得有选择地与 ISP 合作。不过，我们仍在努力把缓存设备部署到尽可能多的 ISP，

cues.en: even to the point of downsizing our caches so that there are better fits for smaller ISPs too.
cues.zh: 甚至还缩小了缓存设备的规格，让它们也更适合规模较小的 ISP。

cues.en: But it also goes for the large ISPs. Verizon,
cues.zh: 但这同样适用于大型 ISP。Verizon、

cues.en: Comcast, all those kind of places, we desperately want to get our cashes into their borders because it saves us money and saves them money. Unfortunately,
cues.zh: Comcast，所有这类地方，我们迫切想把缓存放进他们的边界内，因为这对我们省钱，对他们也省钱。不幸的是，

cues.en: that's not really in their business plans and
cues.zh: 这并不真正在他们的商业计划中，

cues.en: can talk about that a little bit later too.
cues.zh: 这个我们稍后也可以再谈一点。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: this hardware that we have,
cues.zh: 我们拥有的这些硬件，

cues.en: we build our own boxes and we have some design considerations.
cues.zh: 我们自己制造设备，有一些设计上的考量。

cues.en: First and foremost is that our
cues.zh: 首先也是最重要的，是我们的

cues.en: library of titles just in North America is
cues.zh: 片库，仅北美地区就

cues.en: along the size of like two petabytes of
cues.zh: 大约有两拍字节的

cues.en: data.
cues.zh: 数据。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: we wanted to
cues.zh: 我们想要

cues.en: design boxes that could hold as much of the data as possible and be very effective at it, be high density.
cues.zh: 设计出能容纳尽可能多数据、效率很高、密度也很高的存储盒。

cues.en: Along with that, we decided that we were not gonna use any RAID at all because RAID just basically cuts into how much capacity you can put into a box. And you might think that's counterintuitive, well if a disk dies,
cues.zh: 除此之外，我们决定完全不使用 RAID，因为 RAID 会直接减少一个存储盒能容纳的容量。你可能觉得这不合常理：如果一块硬盘坏了，

cues.en: we find it's actually more effective to have redundancy happen at the per server level than inside the server box.
cues.zh: 我们发现，把冗余放在服务器级别，比放在服务器内部更有效。

cues.en: So if a disk dies, the clients that were taking the tiles off that disk just get redirected to another box that has those tiles also
cues.zh: 所以如果一块磁盘坏了，之前从那块磁盘读取分片的客户端会被重定向到另一台也存有这些分片的机器

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: we don't lose any,
cues.zh: 我们不会丢失任何数据，

cues.en: we're not building overhead into our design just to have mirrors or parity volumes or that kind of thing.
cues.zh: 我们不会为了做镜像或奇偶校验卷之类的而给设计增加额外开销。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: that really drove a lot of our considerations. Another thing,
cues.zh: 这确实驱动了我们很多考量。另一件事，

cues.en: we're trying to operate very modestly in terms of power budget and heat budget. We're trying to make these
cues.zh: 我们在功耗和散热预算上尽量做得非常克制。我们想让这些

cues.en: boxes be something that's very friendly to an ISP. It's not drawing a thousand watts and
cues.zh: 机器对ISP非常友好。它不是要消耗一千瓦

cues.en: requiring massive amounts of cooling one to be just another server that they put into the racks.
cues.zh: 需要大量散热，才能作为他们放进机架的另一台服务器。

cues.en: Likewise, for the interchanges and for the racks that we own, we don't want to pay a whole lot of money for power. So we're using modest CPUs, we're not using the
cues.zh: 同样，对于我们拥有的交换机和机架，我们不想在电力上花太多钱。所以我们用的是性能适中的 CPU，不用

cues.en: most powerful
cues.zh: 最强的

cues.en: e7
cues.zh: e7

cues.en: four gigahertz whatever.
cues.zh: 四 GHz 之类的处理器。

cues.en: We're trying to be modest about that. That really constrains our software in a lot of ways that we have to design around.
cues.zh: 我们尽量控制这方面的开销。这在很多方面限制了我们的软件设计，我们必须围绕这些限制来设计。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: we're trying to be efficient with network ports.
cues.zh: 我们也尽量节省网络端口。

cues.en: We designed these boxes to be plugged into 10 gigabit fiber ports.
cues.zh: 我们设计这些设备时，考虑的是接入 10 千兆光纤端口。

cues.en: NICs the box are cheap.
cues.zh: 这些盒子里的网卡很便宜。

cues.en: Fiber switches and fiber routers are very expensive.
cues.zh: 光纤交换机和光纤路由器非常贵。

cues.en: So we try and design our boxes to be as efficient and effective as possible in terms of being able to serve clients, serve
